tkua-frankrig-b31-241.summary: Johan Zobel, Danish resident in Paris, tells Christian IV in cipher that 'D.' has an eye on 'H.', whose arms are fortunate; that he handed over the letters on the protection of the town of Stralsund; that the king should call Zobel home for a talk; that the investiture of Wallenstein with Mecklenburg cannot please the king; and that good people would risk a black eye to put Duke Frederick back in his bishoprics. Written four months after the peace of Lubeck; the cover letters are not solved.
tkua-frankrig-b31-241.en:
By the contributor (Malcolm McBratney, issue #456). Capitals mark the translation of the 19 cipher words; (?) is his doubt about the clear text.
D., H., G., B., Bp., Bo. are Zobel's cover letters; "G. = Christian IV" is from context, the others are the contributor's guesses (D. France, H. Sweden, B. the Emperor), not proved from this sheet.

Most serene, most mighty King, most gracious Lord. For a good while I have noticed that D. has cast a particular eye on H. and holds that those ARMS are fortunate and well worth seconding. I could say neither yes nor no to this; but as long as G. was engaged in war I did not thwart that intention, and held that H. was rightly to be upheld, so that the burden might the sooner come off G.'s neck. For that reason too, concerning the PROTECTION of the TOWN OF STRALSUND, I handed over the letters and humbly let G. know that it was done.

system: Each cipher word begins with an index number 28-39 that selects one of four number alphabets for the 24 letters (straight 4-27, reversed 27-4, and two tables with partly rising, partly falling values); the letters are the figures 4-27.
